item.text: I’ll inspect the monitor implementation and preserve the existing batch analyzer unchanged, then test the stdin contract across mixed formats, boundaries, malformed lines, and no-match cases.

The monitor is currently only a stdin drain. I’m implementing an EOF-time correlator that retains only deployment drop candidates and matching application-error candidates, so unrelated and malformed input cannot produce output.

item.command:
/bin/bash -lc "python3 - <<'PY'
import json, subprocess, sys
monitor = [sys.executable, 'monitor/monitor.py']
# Deliberately out of input order; includes both inclusive boundaries and exclusions.
data = '''malformed junk
2025-04-17T16:00:00+02:00 [ERROR] application request_id=zero release_id=r1 code=UNDEFINED_COLUMN message=\"column target_col does not exist\"
2025-04-17T14:01:30Z [ERROR] application request_id=edge release_id=r1 code=UNDEFINED_COLUMN message=\"column target_col does not exist\"
2025-04-17T14:01:30.001Z [ERROR] application request_id=late release_id=r1 code=UNDEFINED_COLUMN message=\"column target_col does not exist\"
2025-04-17T13:59:59.999Z [ERROR] application request_id=early release_id=r1 code=UNDEFINED_COLUMN message=\"column target_col does not exist\"
2025-04-17T14:00:30Z [ERROR] application request_id=wrong release_id=r2 code=UNDEFINED_COLUMN message=\"column target_col does not exist\"
2025-04-17T14:00:45Z [ERROR] application request_id=wrongcol release_id=r1 code=UNDEFINED_COLUMN message=\"column other_col does not exist\"
2025-04-17T14:00:40Z [ERROR] application request_id=edge release_id=r1 code=UNDEFINED_COLUMN message=\"column target_col does not exist\"
{\"event\":\"SCHEMA_CHANGE\",\"operation\":\"ALTER TABLE things DROP COLUMN target_col\",\"release\":\"r1\",\"service\":\"deployment\",\"severity\":\"INFO\",\"timestamp\":\"2025-04-17T14:00:00Z\"}
{\"event\":\"SCHEMA_CHANGE\",\"operation\":\"ALTER TABLE old DROP COLUMN unused\",\"release\":\"old\",\"service\":\"deployment\",\"severity\":\"INFO\",\"timestamp\":\"2025-04-17T13:00:00Z\"}
'''
result = subprocess.run(monitor, input=data, text=True, capture_output=True, check=True)
assert result.stderr == ''
assert result.stdout.endswith('\\n') and result.stdout.count('\\n') == 1
alert = json.loads(result.stdout)
assert list(alert) == ['release_id', 'column', 'causal_timestamp', 'first_application_error_timestamp', 'affected_request_count']
assert alert == {
 'release_id':'r1', 'column':'target_col',
 'causal_timestamp':'2025-04-17T14:00:00.000Z',
 'first_application_error_timestamp':'2025-04-17T14:00:00.000Z',
 'affected_request_count':2,
}, alert
none = subprocess.run(monitor, input='bad\\n', text=True, capture_output=True, check=True)
assert none.stdout == '' and none.stderr == ''
print('synthetic boundary/no-output checks passed')
PY
{
  sed -n '175000p' inputs/logs/deployment.log
  gzip -cd inputs/logs/application.log.gz | rg 'release_id=2025\\.04\\.17\\.3'
} | python3 monitor/monitor.py"

item.text: The monitor now emits the expected alert for the real incident: release `2025.04.17.3`, column `customer_status`, causal raw instant `14:08:00Z`, first application error `14:08:12Z`, and three distinct affected requests. Boundary tests confirm both 0 and 90 seconds are included and 90.001 seconds is excluded.
